messages:
joel: Quick heads-up — I ran a focused load probe comparing replay traffic vs synthetic heartbeat load for our prefix prefetcher. Results look...weird.

rita: What weird means — lower hitrate or correctness flakiness?

joel: Both, kinda. Under the replay harness (mix of long-tail prefixes) hitrate stabilizes at ~72% after 20k requests. Under synthetic heartbeat (steady short prefixes) it climbs to 92% much faster. Suspect race in warmup path + our kernel selection switching at seq_len boundary.

ken: Can you paste the commands you used? I want to reproduce locally.

joel: Sure — replay harness run:```./tools/replay_harness --trace traces/2025-11-02-replay.json --concurrency 48 --burst 1000 --measure-kv```heartbeat probe:```./tools/heartbeat_load --prefix-dist short --qps 2000 --measure-kv```

maya: Did you toggle batching heuristics or kernel swap? Those can change execution timing and KV priming order.

joel: I tested three variants: default batching, aggressive-batch (lower latency SLO), and batching off. Aggressive-batch increases throughput but introduced a small 1-2% drop in early warmup hitrate on replay.

rita: Any stack or trace that points to eviction vs missing prefetch?

joel: Collected perf traces and a small flamegraph. Main observation: under replay we see many concurrent prefix lookups for the same keyspace with interleaved kernel swaps. Evictions spike when kernel-swap occurs mid-prefetch, and the prefetch writes lose ordering -> effectively a missed warmup.

ken: Do we have a minimized reproducer? Maybe reduce concurrency and artificially trigger kernel swap during warmup. I can try a run with `--kernel-prefer=mini` to avoid swapping and compare.

joel: Good idea. I did one: with `--kernel-prefer=mini` hitrate after 5k requests jumped from 65% -> 88% on replay. Suggests kernel selection is interfering with the KV write path.

perf-bot: Perf summary: replay (concurrency=48) default: hitrate=72%, p95 latency=86ms, eviction-rate=0.018 rps; replay + kernel-prefer=mini: hitrate=88%, p95=92ms; heartbeat: hitrate=92%, p95=45ms.

maya: That's interesting — lower p95 for heartbeat but higher hitrate too. So replay shapes cause both higher latency and lower warmup. Could be ordering + inflight eviction.

rita: We should check correctness under concurrency: are we seeing stale reads or races? Any consistency errors?

joel: No correctness regressions observed (all checksums matched), but we did see 'orphaned' prefetch entries that were evicted before commit, resulting in misses but not inconsistent outputs.

ken: Could we add sequence-numbered prefetch commits so eviction can't remove an entry until commit observed? That has memory cost but might fix warmup flakiness.

maya: Also consider an adaptive prefetch backoff when kernel-swap detected — slow down prefetch during swap windows so we don't thrash the LRU.

rita: For next steps: (1) ken to run minimized reproducer with `--kernel-prefer=mini` and `--kernel-prefer=max` and capture flamegraphs, (2) joel to add instrumentation for prefetch commit/evict ordering (per-prefix counters), (3) maya to prototype adaptive backoff.

ken: I'll run `--concurrency 12/24/48` sweep and push traces to s3://redwood-perf/kv-prefetch/1845678901/ by EOD.

joel: Pushed logs and a small sample trace (link: https://s3.redwood.internal/kv-prefetch/1845678901/sample.trace). Trace includes a short annotated timeline: kernel-swap events, prefetch start/commit.

perf-bot: Regression ticket created: PERF-1248 — "KV prefetch warmup race under kernel swap". Priority: P2.

maya: Thanks — if anyone finds anything surprising in the sweeps ping me. I'm going to sketch an adaptive backoff algorithm that detects swap churn via a short moving window of kernel-change events.

joel: One more note: please ensure apples-to-apples comparison — same seed for replay and same randomization for synthetic. I used seed=98321 for all runs.

rita: Good call. Keep updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
